why_angle: Of the cited rival pages that could be read, Wirecutter gives the Mars 3's lumens ('over 800') and runtimes, and none of them turns any pick's lumens into on-screen foot-lamberts or says how large a screen each one can light to the 16 ft-L cinema target. This page does that for all four picks, using ProjectorCentral and Laurent Willen measurements, and adds Soundcore's own battery-mode lumen ratings for the Mars 3 (700 lm for 1 h 30 min, 300 lm for 5 h). The RTINGS pages returned only navigation and Yahoo/Forbes returned 403, so those could not be checked.

page.title: Best Smart Projector for Outdoor Movies, by Screen Size
page.h1: Best smart projector for outdoor movies: how big a screen each one can light
page.desc: Measured lumens converted to on-screen brightness: the Nebula X1 lights a 215-inch screen to cinema level, while the battery-powered Mars 3 tops out near 120 inches.
page.answer: Short answer. The best smart projector for outdoor movies is the Nebula X1: in Movie mode its measured brightness, 2,193 lumens, gives about 51 ft-L on a 120-inch screen and fills up to 215 inches at 16 ft-L. The battery-powered Mars 3 reaches 16 ft-L only up to 120 inches.

page.after:
What the differences mean

On-screen brightness is lumens × screen gain ÷ screen area in square feet, measured in foot-lamberts (ft-L). A 120-inch 16:9 screen is 42.73 sq ft and a 150-inch one is 66.76 sq ft. Every figure here assumes a gain-1.0 screen and Movie mode, the mode you would watch a film in. The SMPTE cinema target is 16 ft-L, within an allowed range of 12–22. ProjectorCentral suggests about 50 ft-L for a room with some light, which is closer to a backyard with porch lights or lit windows nearby.

  • Nebula X1: 2,193 ÷ 42.73 = 51.3 ft-L at 120 in; 2,193 ÷ 66.76 = 32.8 ft-L at 150 in.
  • XGIMI Horizon 20: 1,682 ÷ 42.73 = 39.4 ft-L at 120 in; 1,682 ÷ 66.76 = 25.2 ft-L at 150 in.
  • Nebula Cosmos 4K SE: 1,298 ÷ 42.73 = 30.4 ft-L at 120 in; 1,298 ÷ 66.76 = 19.4 ft-L at 150 in.
  • Nebula Mars 3: 686 ÷ 42.73 = 16.1 ft-L at 120 in; 686 ÷ 66.76 = 10.3 ft-L at 150 in, below the 12 ft-L floor.
  • Largest screen at 16 ft-L: diagonal = √(lumens ÷ 16 × 144 ÷ 0.4273). For the X1, √(137.1 × 337) = 215 in.
  • Measured against rated: X1 2,193 ÷ 3,500 = 63%; Cosmos 4K SE 1,298 ÷ 1,800 = 72%; Mars 3 686 ÷ 1,000 = 69%.
Your setupFitsWhy

How big a screen each one lights, on wall power and on battery

The Mars 3 on battery. Soundcore's battery-life table rates the Mars 3 at 700 lumens for 1 h 30 min in Standard mode on battery, and 300 lumens for 5 h in Eco. An optional brightness setting switches it to Eco as soon as you unplug the adapter. ProjectorCentral measured 261 lumens in Movie mode and 442 in Bright mode in Eco. That reaches 16 ft-L only up to about 74 and 96 inches. So the 5-hour figure applies to a picture of roughly 100 inches or smaller after full dark, and 1 h 30 min at Standard brightness is shorter than most feature films. {buy:nebula-mars-3}

Plug-in projectors without an outlet. Notebookcheck measured the X1 at about 160 W at its highest brightness, which is 0.32 kWh for a 2-hour film (160 × 2). Notebookcheck says a 500 Wh power station covers most outdoor movie nights. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 holds 1,024 Wh, so 1,024 ÷ 160 = 6.4 h before inverter losses. {buy:bluetti-elite-100-v2} Laurent Willen measured the Horizon 20 at 97 W at laser level 10, so 1,024 ÷ 97 = 10.6 h before losses. XGIMI rates it at no more than 180 W.

Brightest modes. In Conference mode, ProjectorCentral measured the X1 at 3,187 lumens. Laurent Willen measured the Horizon 20's High Power mode at 3,020 lumens (70.7 ft-L at 120 in), at a measured contrast of 1,304:1. Both are options for a twilight start, before the sky is fully dark.

Streaming. Nebula's spec sheets list both the X1 and the Cosmos 4K SE as Google TV with Official Netflix. On the Mars 3, Soundcore's support article says Netflix is a mobile build installed through the Nebula Play app, and you control it in mouse mode from the phone app. If Netflix is your main service, plug a streaming stick into the Mars 3's HDMI port.

Not recommended

The Nebula Mars 3 for a 150-inch screen. Its measured 686 lumens in Movie mode give 10.3 ft-L at 150 inches, below the 12 ft-L floor. Even its Bright mode (959 lumens) gives only 14.4 ft-L. On battery in Eco, the most it can light to 16 ft-L is a 74-inch picture. For a 150-inch backyard screen, choose one of the plug-in projectors and add a power station where there is no outlet.
